title: A child who cannot settle
body: Rohan, aged eight, is in Class 3. His teacher notes that he rarely stays in his seat, interrupts others, and loses track of instructions within a minute or two. He reads below the level of his classmates, yet a psychologist's assessment shows that his intelligence is in the normal range. At home his parents find it hard to get him to finish any task, and other children often avoid playing with him. The school counsellor suggests a programme in which Rohan earns small rewards for finishing short, carefully structured tasks with immediate feedback, and is taught to say to himself 'stop, think, and then do' before acting.

title: Painting a landscape
body: Anya, an art student, is painting a landscape on a flat canvas. She draws two rail tracks that come closer and closer until they meet at a point on the horizon. A hut in the foreground partly hides a tree behind it. The hills at the back are painted hazy and bluish, while the trees near the front are crisp and clear. On the path, she paints pebbles large and widely spaced near the bottom of the canvas, and smaller and more densely packed as the path goes towards the horizon. When she checks the painting from across the room, it gives a strong impression of depth even though the canvas is completely flat.
